continuity.arc_goal: Produce a solid, internally consistent RFC for State Graph and Links that covers core semantics (links, workflow lifecycle with linked children, content-addressable frozen graphs) and composition patterns. Success = RFC can be handed to SDK and runtime implementers with no ambiguity.

progress_update.summary: We continued refining the State Graph and Links RFC. Reviewed it end-to-end, identified semantic gaps, and resolved the major ones. Added the workflow returning→completed lifecycle where linked children block parent completion, guaranteeing frozen graphs are fully immutable. Clarified mutability contracts (links as delegated write permission), separated link status from completion handlers, added tree cancellation and timeouts. Then had a design discussion on Promise Objects (objects that freeze and participate in the completion tree) which led to the decision that exclusive shared handlers on workflows cover that use case. Content-addressable frozen state via Merkle trees was added to the core RFC design. Tiered storage deferred.
progress_update.goal: Produce a solid, internally consistent RFC for State Graph and Links that covers the core semantics of links, workflow lifecycle with linked children, content-addressable frozen graphs, and composition patterns. Success = the RFC can be handed to an SDK implementer and a runtime implementer with no ambiguity on the core model.
accomplished: Resolved mutability contract: links are delegated write permission from object to runtime
Added workflow returning→completed lifecycle: linked children block parent completion, full graph freezes atomically
Added workflow tree cancellation (propagates cancel through links) and timeout semantics
Clarified completion handler execution: link status always updated by runtime, handlers queued as normal invocations
Simplified failure propagation: child failure updates link status, parent continues, no automatic propagation
Added content-addressable frozen state (Merkle trees) to the core RFC — root hash seals the entire computation graph
Design discussion on Promise Objects → decided exclusive shared handlers on workflows (Option A) is the path, deferred to future
Updated future_design_ideas with Promise Objects, content-addressable state, and exclusive handler decisions
progress_update.now: Just completed adding content-addressable frozen state to the RFC and recording the exclusive shared handler decision (Option A) as final. RFC is in a solid state for the core semantic model.
next_steps: Wire protocol / journal entry specification for links (deferred until semantics stable, but semantics are now stable)
Cross-partition link design sketch (deferred but acknowledged as common case)
Consider exclusive shared handlers on workflows as an RFC addition or separate RFC
Implementation planning for link storage in partition store
constraints: Focus on semantics first, implementation details later
State Graph RFC stands alone — don't merge with Process Composition RFC
Failure propagation strategies deferred to future RFC
Tiered storage for frozen graphs deferred
Promise Objects deferred until linked workflow model is proven
decisions: Links are delegated write permission — object authorizes runtime to update link status on workflow completion
Workflow completion requires all linked children to complete recursively (returning→completed lifecycle)
Result is not observable until full completion
Child failure does NOT kill parent — link status updates, parent continues
Content-addressable frozen state (Merkle trees) is core design, not deferred
Exclusive shared handlers on workflows (Option A: queued, run when run is suspended) is the decided path for interactive workflows
Promise Objects deferred — exclusive shared handlers cover the use case
Graph curation is load-bearing — unlinked children don't block completion
open_questions: Should workflows have a default timeout or is no-timeout the default?
Link storage model: same column family as state or separate?
When exactly is the Merkle tree computed? (noted as implementation detail to defer)
Returning state: should it be observable to SSE clients or hidden?
risks: The two RFCs (State Graph vs Process Composition) have diverging models — may confuse future readers
Cross-partition links are deferred but most cross-service links will be cross-partition
